items.title: John Pizzarelli, Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 29, 2000 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Like when you hear his group with John Bunch and Jay Leonhart, that’s the only group I want to go hear.

ctx.x: Yeah. That’s what I used to do a lot. I used to think I was having fun dropping beats. That was — my Bill Evans friends used to make me screw the time up all the time. But the best one is “Contrasts” I think. And we never got something that was representative of what we were doing for those ten years. But I think “Contrasts,” the newest one that we made for Arbors, which is just the two of us, came out last year, is more of us both as musicians. This is more Bucky’s leader and I do what I do. But it’s funny to…

that. And then he started to play “Nuages” and he’s looking at me like, “you going to play now?” I’m going I ain’t going to play. You play. You go. You play. You’re on. And he’s best when he’s been playing over a long period of time. Like when you hear his group with John Bunch and Jay Leonhart, that’s the only group I want to go hear. And they don’t play any songs that anybody else in playing. I mean they’re playing “Shakey Breaks The Ice” from the Joe Mooney group, they’re playing Fritz Kreisler, swinging the…

items.title: John Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 18, 2023 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: But then when he worked with John Bunch and Jay Leonhart

ctx.x: Well you know I think that’s — you know I think I still border on the shtick but I’ve gotten a little better at it, at the important times anyway. I mean I like the idea of, you know we used to joke with Bucky about, you know could you at least tell us what the next song is? Could we have a clue? Will you let us in? You know when he would do solo concerts when I was between ten and fifteen. But then when he worked with John Bunch and Jay Leonhart, they would let — Bucky would talk for a while and then he’d say,…
that stemmed out. And I think the other part was I like to tell little stories about the things that connected the dots a little bit.
